GREEN PLC CLINIC - DISCHARGE SUMMARY
Patient: Joshua Dorsey DOB: 12/23/1993 Sex: M MRN: 707261
Admit: 04/23/2026 Discharge: 04/24/2026

Principal diagnosis: Asthma
Secondary diagnosis: Pulmonary sarcoidosis

Admitting diagnosis: Upper Respiratory Infection (URI)
Discharge diagnosis: Upper Respiratory Infection (URI) superimposed on controlled Asthma and Pulmonary sarcoidosis

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS:
Mr. Joshua Dorsey, a 33-year-old male, presented to the clinic on 04/23/2026 with complaints of cough, nasal congestion, and mild fever for 3 days, consistent with a URI. The patient reported no significant increase in asthma symptoms but was concerned about the URI exacerbating his underlying conditions.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY:
1. Asthma: Diagnosed on 01/16/2016, currently controlled with daily controller medications and requires approximately 2 steroid bursts per year. Patient is also on biologic therapy.
2. Pulmonary sarcoidosis: Diagnosed on 09/29/2023, condition has been stable the past 1.6 years.

MEDICATIONS ON ADMISSION:
- budesonide-formoterol 160/4.5 mcg inhaler, 2 puffs twice daily
- montelukast 10 mg tablet, once daily at bedtime

ALLERGIES: None reported

SOCIAL HISTORY:
The patient reports consuming approximately 10 alcoholic drinks per week. He denies any tobacco use. 

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS:
- Constitutional: Mild fever, fatigue
- HEENT: Nasal congestion, no sore throat
- Respiratory: Cough, no wheezing or shortness of breath
- Cardiovascular: No chest pain or palpitations
- Gastrointestinal: No nausea, vomiting, or diarrhea
- Musculoskeletal: No joint pain or muscle aches
- Neurological: No headaches or dizziness
- Skin: No rashes or lesions

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION ON ADMISSION:
- Vital signs: Blood pressure 131/82 mmHg, heart rate 78 bpm, respiratory rate 18 breaths per minute, temperature 37.8°C, weight 167 lbs.
- General: Alert, oriented, and in no acute distress
- HEENT: Normocephalic, atraumatic. Nasal erythematous, clear rhinorrhea.
- Neck: Supple, no lymphadenopathy
- Chest: Clear to auscultation bilaterally, no wheezes, rales, or rhonchi
- Heart: Regular rate and rhythm, no murmurs, rubs, or gallops
- Abdomen: Soft, non-tender, no Extremities: No edema, cyanosis, or clubbing
- Skin: Warm and dry, no rashes

HOSPITAL COURSE:
The patient was admitted for observation and management of his URI. He was kept nil per os (NPO) initially and started on supportive care including hydration and antipyretics as needed. His asthma and pulmonary sarcoidosis remained stable throughout the admission. He did not req

uire any additional respiratory treatments or interventions. His symptoms gradually improved the next 24 hours, and he was deemed fit for discharge.

PROCEDURES:
No procedures were performed during this admission.

DISCHARGE MEDICATIONS:
- budesonide-formoterol 160/4.5 mcg inhaler, 2 puffs twice daily
- montelukast 10 mg tablet, once daily at bedtime

DISCHARGE INSTRUCTIONS:
The patient was advised to continue his current medications for asthma and to complete any prescribed course of antibiotics if initiated (none in this case). He was encouraged to increase fluid intake, use humidification, and rest as needed. He was instructed to follow up with his pulmonologist in 1-2 weeks or sooner if symptoms worsen.

FOLLOW-UP:
The patient is scheduled to follow up Dr. Kyle Fox, his pulmonologist at Green PLC Clinic, in 1-2 weeks for a post-discharge evaluation. He was instructed to return to the emergency department if he experiences worsening symptoms, difficulty breathing, chest pain, or any other concerning symptoms.

CONDITION ON DISCHARGE:
The patient was discharged in stable condition with resolution of his URI symptoms. His asthma and pulmonary sarcoidosis remained well-controlled throughout the admission.

FINAL DIAGNOSES:
1. Upper Respiratory Infection (URI)
2. Asthma, controlled
3. Pulmonary sarcoidosis, stable

This discharge summary was prepared by Dr. Kyle Fox, Pulmonologist at Green PLC Clinic.
